text.p: Lead rallied strongly on the London Metals Exchange, but other metals were mainly softer. Gold strengthened, wheat closed mixed and oil eased further. The CRB index was down 0.31 at 242.41.

METALS - Lead clung tightly to most of its gains on Friday from a blistering rally which propelled prices above $700 at one point. Lead prices ended the London Metal Exchange (LME) afternoon kerb at $698 per tonne, a gain of $23 versus Thursday's finish. Options related buying, fund shortcovering and tight April dates were responsible for the metal's dramatic surge, traders said.
Copper intially dipped to a low of $2,362, from Thursday's kerb close of $2,393, after LME stocks came in down an expected 3,475 tonnes. But prices bounced up to finish the kerb at $2,378.
Aluminium was underpinned by a substantial LME stock decline of 11,075 tonnes on Friday morning. However, it failed to move out of a narrow range and ended the kerb just $2 firmer at $1,654.
Nickel repeated Thursday's strong close of $8,070 against a backdrop of continued concerns about possible labour unrest in Russia's Norilsk Nickel factory.
Tin closed nearly $100 down at $5,790, compared to $5,880 on Thursday. A stocks rise of 170 tonnes did little to improve the market's sluggish tone.
Zinc held steady most of the day and made a halfhearted attempt to push higher at the afternoon kerb. But the effort fell flat and the metal finished at $1,218, down $9.
Alloy was last indicated at $1,540/45 versus $1,550.

CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby March higher on bull spreading with some citing arbitrage buying from the options pit as rationale for a portion of the late rally, traders said. Wheat futures closed 4-3/4 cents per bushel higher to three lower, with March up 4-3/4 at $3.73.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Friday, except for palladium, after the complex recovered from a midday dip. Weakness in US stocks and bonds provided some support for hard assets, analysts said. COMEX April gold settled up $4.10 an ounce at $365.10, after seeing a session high at $365.50, the highest level seen since January 3.

NYMEX crude ended the month of February on Friday with the lowest settlement since late July after selling accelerated in late session when key technical support was breached, traders said. April crude ended 59 cents off at $20.30 a barrel, prompt crude's lowest settlement since July 29, 1996 when it closed at $20.28.

CSCE world sugar futures closed higher in volatile trade as the nearby spread swelled to a 0.40 cent premium in March before ending at a 0.35 cent premium. The spot month went off the board at 11.32 cents per lb, up 0.27 cent from the previous close. raders said speculative short-covering in the now-expired March contract coupled with producer activity on both sides of the market in May accounted for the bulk of the day's estimated volume at 22,596 lots.
